title: Knowledge Check 6 - Lessons 26-30
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 26-30 - Harmonization and Unification. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: Which statement best describes what identity resolution produces when it unifies profiles?
options: A golden record that replaces the values in the source systems
A unified profile that acts as a system of reference, with unified links back to the source records
A copy of whichever source record has the highest priority
A list of suspected duplicates for an admin to merge manually
questions.explanation: Unification produces a unified profile that unlocks source data through unified links, and it never overwrites source records. The golden-record option is the strongest distractor because reconciliation does pick a displayed value, but that value is only what the unified profile shows, not a replacement of source data.

questions.question: A consultant is asked to explain determinism in unification. Which statement is accurate?
options: Two runs over the same source data and ruleset produce the same groupings
The result varies each run because matching is probabilistic
Determinism means the source records are permanently merged
Determinism means reconciliation rewrites every conflicting field at the source
questions.explanation: Determinism means the same input data and ruleset yield the same groupings, which makes results reproducible and auditable. The probabilistic option is wrong because fuzzy methods compare values but the ruleset logic still produces the same matches for the same data.

questions.question: Unification produces several unified profiles that actually belong to one customer. Which downstream effect most directly results?
options: Source records are permanently deleted from the source systems
Segment counts and activation sends inflate because the customer appears as several members
Reconciliation rules stop running
Match rules are automatically loosened by the platform
questions.explanation: When matching is too strict, one person appears as multiple unified profiles, so segments over count and activations send duplicates. Deletion is wrong because unification never changes source data, and the platform does not loosen rules on its own.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the unification process?
options: Match, harmonize and map, reconcile, unify
Harmonize and map, match, reconcile, produce unified profiles
Reconcile, match, harmonize and map, unify
Unify, match, reconcile, harmonize and map
questions.explanation: Unification maps sources to the data model first, matches profiles into groups, reconciles the displayed values, and then produces unified profiles and links. Reversing mapping and matching is the strongest distractor but fails because match rules can only see mapped fields.

questions.question: A unified profile shows one value for First Name while the contributing sources disagree. What decided that value?
options: The match rule with the highest criteria count
The reconciliation rule assigned to the field, such as Last Updated or Source Priority
The order in which data streams ran
The data space assignment
questions.explanation: Reconciliation resolves a single value conflict for a unified field by field, using rules such as Last Updated, Most Frequent, or Source Priority. Match criteria only decide whether records link, and they do not choose which value displays.

questions.question: Which statement about reconciliation is TRUE?
options: It updates the connected source systems with the winning value
It determines only what the unified profile displays and never changes source data
It applies to email and phone contact points as well
It runs before match rules and groups the records
questions.explanation: Reconciliation selects the displayed value for the unified profile and does not change source systems. The contact point option is wrong because reconciliation does not apply to contact points, and it runs after matching, not before.

questions.question: A ruleset has one match rule with two criteria. When does it link two source profiles?
options: When either criterion is satisfied
When both criteria are satisfied
When the first criterion is satisfied and the second is ignored
Only when a reconciliation rule also matches
questions.explanation: Criteria within a single match rule are combined with AND, so both must be satisfied for that rule to link profiles. The strongest distractor, either criterion, would be correct only if the two criteria were split into two separate rules.

questions.question: Which statement about reconciliation and contact points is correct?
options: Reconciliation keeps one email and discards the others
Reconciliation does not apply to contact points, so all emails and phones remain on the unified profile
Contact points must be reconciled before they appear on a profile
Reconciliation deletes duplicate phone numbers from the source
questions.explanation: Reconciliation is excluded from contact points, so every email and phone stays on the unified profile and source priority in activation decides which is delivered. Discarding or deleting contact points describes behavior the platform does not perform.

questions.question: An identifier field is populated differently across several sources, and the customer wants a stable ID on the unified profile. Which reconciliation rule fits best?
options: Most Frequent
Source Priority applied to the ID field
Last Updated
Ignore Empty Values only
questions.explanation: Reconciliation guidance recommends Source Priority for ID fields so the identifier stays stable and drawn from the highest priority source. Most Frequent could shift the ID as data changes, and Last Updated would make the ID change whenever any source updates.

questions.question: A customer ingests data from a single source system and asks whether to run unification. What is the best guidance?
options: Unify anyway so future sources match more easily
Unification is not justified without a cross source use case, since it adds cost and governance burden for little benefit
Unification is required by every Data 360 license
Unify only after activating the segment
questions.explanation: Unification earns its cost when one customer view must be assembled across sources; a single source already has one record per customer. The future-sources option is the strongest distractor but building unification with no present benefit is the wrong default, and no license mandates it.

questions.question: Why is consent a first order concern in a unification design?
options: Unification encrypts source data automatically
Combining data across sources can create inferences and uses beyond the original consent, so permitted purposes and data spaces must be confirmed
Reconciliation removes records that lack consent
Consent applies only to phone numbers
questions.explanation: Because a unified profile aggregates data across systems, the combination can create inferences and uses the customer never consented to, so the consultant must confirm permitted purposes and use data spaces as boundaries. Reconciliation does not filter on consent, and consent is not limited to phone.

questions.question: Which activation membership avoids duplicate counts for a unified customer?
options: The source Individual data model object
The Unified Individual data model object
The raw data lake object
The Contact Point Email object
questions.explanation: Using Unified Individual as the activation membership counts one row per unified profile, while the source Individual object can produce duplicate entries. Data lake and contact point objects are not memberships that represent the unified customer.

questions.question: Which object is the central who of the Customer 360 data model, and what must person-related objects map to for identity resolution to work?
options: Unified Link Individual
Individual via the Individual ID field
Account
Individual Identity Link
questions.explanation: Individual is the hub and imported customer identifiers must be mapped to Individual ID to drive identity resolution and accurate segments. The unified objects are outputs after matching, and Account and the link object are not the central who.

questions.question: A marketing team wants to store each customer's email address and phone number as separate, addressable channels. Which object family fits?
options: Engagement objects
Account Contact
Contact point objects such as Contact Point Email and Contact Point Phone, linked to Individual through Party
Party Identification
questions.explanation: Each contact point object holds one channel identifier and links back to Individual, so email and phone belong in their contact point objects. Engagement objects are interactions, Account Contact is a role object, and Party Identification holds identifiers such as a license number.

questions.question: A Product Order Engagement record is an interaction. Which object does it reference to tie the order interaction back to a person?
options: Individual, through the Individual ID reference
Sales Order Product as the source table
Contact Point Address
Unified Individual only
questions.explanation: Engagement objects are event-like and tie back to the Individual through an Individual ID reference. The source order table is not the model link, contact point objects hold handles not interactions, and unified objects are produced after matching.
